source_text: Sic enim Apostolus ad Corinthios: Nam sicut mulier - inquit - ex viro, ita et vir per mulierem, omnia autem ex Deo [n121] . Tertio vero ostendit ratio, quoniam, etsi neutrum horum, quod nobis amminiculatur, fuisset, tamen illam sententiam, qua per unum hominem intrasse peccatum in hunc mundum Paulus disputat, nullum cum Manichaeis inisse foedus.
pass_a_gloss: For thus the Apostle to the Corinthians: For as the woman, he says, from the man, so also the man through the woman, but all things from God. Thirdly however reason has shown that, even if neither of these which assists us had been, nevertheless that sentence by which Paul disputes that through one human sin entered into this world had entered no treaty with the Manichaeans.

lemmas.lexica: Blaise Manichaeus; Julian's polemic label vs natural evil
LS peccatum=fault, error; Blaise Christian sin
LS ratio; Blaise use of reason required for sin

pass_b_english: Thus the apostle says to the Corinthians: ‘Just as woman is from man, so man is through woman; but all things are from God’ (1 Corinthians 11:12). Thirdly, reason shows that even if neither of the two supporting points we offered existed, Paul’s statement that sin entered this world through one man would still have formed no alliance with the Manichaeans.

choices.why: Julian's standing charge: natural evil is Manichaean. Keep the sect-name, not 'dualists'.
Julian's forensic/moral fault tied to will, not a substance in nature.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

bible_refs.note: Repeats or discusses sin entering or passing through one man.
From Pass B Scripture tagging; wording follows Julian's Latin, not a modern Bible.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
